keyTerms.definition: Answer keys that accompany the U09 lesson file in the course.
Answers provided without access to notes or other materials.
The file name given to the U09 lesson answer keys.
A page option used to track progress through the section.

recall.question: What date is listed for the Unit 09 Keys page?
recall.answer: The date listed is 2026-10-06.

recall.question: Are the U09 lesson answer keys open-book or closed-book?
recall.answer: They are closed-book answers.

recall.question: Where should the answer keys file be kept?
recall.answer: It should be kept separate from the lesson file.

keyTerms.definition: A parallelism strategy that uses 8 full copies and splits data across them.
A parallelism strategy that splits stages and uses whole layers.

recall.question: What splitting approach does the Pipeline parallelism strategy use?
recall.answer: Pipeline parallelism splits stages and uses whole layers for each stage.

keyTerms.definition: DP uses 20 GB of memory per GPU according to the section text.
EP-8 uses 2.5 GB of memory per GPU plus dispatch overhead.

recall.question: How much memory per GPU does DP use compared to TP-8?
recall.answer: DP uses 20 GB per GPU while TP-8 uses only 2.5 GB per GPU.

keyTerms.definition: The cost TP pays by syncing after every matmul.
What multiplies the cost of every sync TP performs.

recall.question: What is the all-reduce tax in TP?
recall.answer: It is the sync that TP performs after every matmul, and the thin link multiplies the cost of each one.

keyTerms.definition: TP/PP/EP still run.

recall.question: The model is 100 GB. Which splits still run on 40 GB GPUs?
recall.answer: DP dies (100 GB > 40 GB). TP/PP/EP at 12.5 GB/GPU still run.

keyTerms.definition: A criterion used to rank measured step times when comparing collective, bubble, and dispatch methods.
Measured durations of individual steps used to rank performance approaches by tax.

recall.question: What does the E05 hypothesis claim about measured step times?
recall.answer: The hypothesis states that measured step times rank by their tax across collective, bubble, and dispatch approaches. The section instructs reporting all four results.

keyTerms.definition: Then all-gather: the two passes.

recall.question: Write the ring formula and name the two passes.
recall.answer: t = 2*(n-1)/n * S/BW. Passes: reduce-scatter, then all-gather.

recall.question: Toy above. Compute t at n=8 and n=64.

keyTerms.definition: Or a degraded link: one slow peer throttles the ring.
One slow peer.

recall.question: The sync takes far longer than the formula. Name two causes.
recall.answer: Incast congestion, or a degraded link (one slow peer throttles the ring).

keyTerms.definition: t falls 4x, linear in S.
The scaling.

recall.question: Gradients compress 4x. What happens to t?
recall.answer: t falls 4x (linear in S).

keyTerms.definition: Slope of all-reduce time vs S.
Report it.

recall.question: State the linear-fit hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: all-reduce time is linear in S with slope 1.75/BW. Report the fit.

keyTerms.definition: A parallelism strategy that this rule says should remain contained within a single node.
A training approach that this rule allows to extend across multiple nodes.

recall.question: According to this rule, where should tensor-parallel groups be kept, and what parallelism may cross nodes?
recall.answer: Tensor-parallel groups should be kept inside the node. Data parallel or pipeline parallelism is allowed to cross nodes.

keyTerms.definition: Intra-node 0.058 s vs split 0.70 s.
Split.

recall.question: Toy above. Compute both times and the ratio.
recall.answer: Intra-node: 0.058 s. Split: 0.70 s. Ratio: 12x.

keyTerms.definition: Every sync crosses the thin link.
The slow interconnect.

recall.question: A tensor-parallel job is much slower than expected. What is the placement?
recall.answer: The TP group is split across nodes. Every sync crosses the thin link.

keyTerms.definition: Placement stops mattering because any split pays the same collective cost.
The total cost stays the same for any split, so placement makes no difference.

recall.question: What does E14 say about placement?
recall.answer: Placement stops mattering. Any split pays the same collective cost.

keyTerms.definition: The measured ratio matches it.
Report both.

recall.question: State the ratio hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: the measured ratio matches BW_in/BW_out. Report both.

keyTerms.definition: max(worker times).
Equals max of worker times.

recall.question: Write the step-time rule.
recall.answer: Step time = max(worker times).

keyTerms.definition: The text states the GPU tax is 40 percent of step time.
The section reports that 28 GPU-seconds are wasted per step.

recall.question: How many GPU-seconds are wasted per step at E17 step 14?
recall.answer: The text reports that 28 GPU-seconds are wasted per step, with a tax of 40 percent.

keyTerms.definition: A degrading GPU or disk whose performance grows worse over time.
The duration each worker takes, checked to spot a growing straggler.

recall.question: What should you check to detect a growing straggler?
recall.answer: Check per-worker times. A degrading GPU or disk shows up as a growing straggler.

keyTerms.definition: The state in which workers train on outdated parameters, which can hurt model convergence.
The stabilization of model parameters during training that can suffer when workers train on old parameters.

recall.question: What is staleness and how does it affect convergence?
recall.answer: Staleness happens when workers train on old parameters. This can cause convergence to suffer.

keyTerms.definition: A small set of workers explains most of it.
Report it.

recall.question: State the tail-attribution hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: a small set of workers explains most of the tail. Report the split.

keyTerms.definition: The text gives E21 Bubble as the expression (p-1)/(m+p-1).
E21 is a label paired with the formula Bubble equals (p-1)/(m+p-1).

recall.question: What is the formula for E21 Bubble?
recall.answer: E21 Bubble equals (p-1)/(m+p-1).

recall.question: Toy above. Compute the bubble at m=8 and m=16.

keyTerms.definition: One processing stage in the pipeline that runs 2x, used here as an example of uneven timing.
The assumption baked into the formula that every stage takes the same amount of time.

recall.question: Why does the formula not match real stage times?
recall.answer: The formula assumed equal stages, but stage times are uneven. The embedding stage runs 2x as an example of this mismatch.

keyTerms.definition: No pipeline at all, just sequential stages (100% bubble).
At m=1.

recall.question: M = 1. What is the pipeline?
recall.answer: m=1: no pipeline at all, just sequential stages (100% bubble).

keyTerms.definition: Follows (p-1)/(m+p-1).
Report it.

recall.question: State the idle-fit hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: idle fraction follows (p-1)/(m+p-1). Report the fit.

keyTerms.definition: ZeRO-1 corresponds to partitioning the optimizer states.
ZeRO-2 adds gradient partitioning to the optimizer states already handled.

recall.question: What does each ZeRO stage add as it progresses from ZeRO-1 to ZeRO-3?
recall.answer: ZeRO-1 partitions optimizer states. ZeRO-2 adds gradients, and ZeRO-3 adds parameters on top of those.

keyTerms.definition: ZeRO-3.
Plain DP.

recall.question: Toy above. Compute per-GPU bytes for ZeRO-3 and plain DP.
recall.answer: ZeRO-3: 20.0 GB/GPU. Plain DP: 160 GB/GPU.

keyTerms.definition: Time cost that dominates when layers are tiny and need splitting across workers.
Communication operation run per layer, whose cost exceeds memory savings for tiny layers.

recall.question: Why does gather latency dominate for tiny layers?
recall.answer: Gather latency dominates for tiny layers because the per-layer all-gather communication costs more than the memory it saves.

keyTerms.definition: Saves nothing with SGD without momentum: a no-op.
No states to shard.

recall.question: Optimizer is SGD (no states). What does ZeRO-1 save?
recall.answer: ZeRO-1 saves nothing (no states to shard). It is a no-op for SGD without momentum.

keyTerms.definition: Step time rises for small layers.
The regime.

recall.question: State the stage-profile hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: memory falls across stages 1/2/3. step time rises at stage 3 for small layers. Report all.

keyTerms.definition: (N/k) * save_cost.
Per-checkpoint cost.

recall.question: Write the overhead formula.
recall.answer: Overhead = (N/k) * save_cost.

keyTerms.definition: 300 s overhead (3%), rework capped at 1000 s.
60 s (0.6%), rework capped at 5000 s.

recall.question: Toy above. Compute overhead and max rework for k=100 and k=500.
recall.answer: k=100: 300 s overhead (3%), rework capped at 1000 s. K=500: 60 s (0.6%), rework capped at 5000 s.

keyTerms.definition: Not saved: resume replays the wrong order.
Also must be saved.

recall.question: Resume diverges from the pre-crash trajectory. What was not saved?
recall.answer: The data-loader state (or RNG state) was not saved. Resume replays the wrong order.

keyTerms.definition: Save every step: overhead zero, rework one step.
The rework.

recall.question: If saving costs nothing, what is the best checkpoint interval?
recall.answer: Save every step. Overhead is zero and rework is one step.

keyTerms.definition: Per-GPU time scales down with shard count.
The scaling knob.

recall.question: State the sharded-save hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: sharded saves scale per-GPU time down with shard count. Report the curve.

keyTerms.definition: Total time to finish all jobs.
GPU-hours idle.

recall.question: Define makespan and waste.
recall.answer: Makespan: total time to finish all jobs. Waste: GPU-hours idle.

keyTerms.definition: The total time E37 takes to run, shown as 2 hours.
Unused GPU hours from E37, shown as 4 GPU-h.

recall.question: What is the makespan of E37 and how much waste does it produce?
recall.answer: The makespan of E37 is 2 hours, with 4 GPU-h of waste.

keyTerms.definition: FIFO without backfill: big jobs block small ones.
The naive scheduler.

recall.question: Small jobs wait forever. What policy causes it?
recall.answer: FIFO without backfill: big jobs block small ones (head-of-line blocking).

keyTerms.definition: Shrink to fill gaps: waste falls, individual jobs slower.
What elastic jobs fill.

recall.question: Jobs are elastic. What changes?
recall.answer: Elastic jobs shrink to fill gaps: waste falls, at the cost of slower individual jobs.

keyTerms.definition: Cuts mean wait vs FIFO.
Report both.

recall.question: State the backfill hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: backfill cuts mean wait vs FIFO. Report both.

keyTerms.definition: preemptions * (interval + resume) / run time.
The count.

recall.question: Write the rework-fraction formula.
recall.answer: Rework fraction = preemptions * (interval + resume) / run time.

keyTerms.definition: Rework with 1 expected preemption.
Expected.

recall.question: Toy above. Compute expected preemptions and rework fraction.
recall.answer: 1 expected preemption. Rework 5.8% of the run.

keyTerms.definition: Preemption rate too high (or correlated): rework exceeds the discount.
What rework must beat.

recall.question: Spot job never finishes. What does the rate look like?
recall.answer: The preemption rate is too high (or correlated): rework exceeds the discount.

keyTerms.definition: One crash loses the whole run.
One crash loses the whole run.

recall.question: Checkpoint interval = run length. What is the risk?
recall.answer: One crash loses the whole run. Maximum risk.

keyTerms.definition: Preemptions are bursty, not Poisson.
The wrong model.

recall.question: State the burstiness hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: preemptions are bursty, not Poisson. Report the fit.

keyTerms.definition: max over resources of demand/total.
Equals max over resources of demand divided by total.

recall.question: Define the dominant share.
recall.answer: Dominant share = max over resources of demand/total.

keyTerms.definition: Dominant shares of A, B, C.
Dominant at 1.0.

recall.question: Toy above. Compute all three shares.

keyTerms.definition: Gaming the dominant-share accounting.
The attack.

recall.question: A user grabs GPUs by inflating another demand. Name the game.
recall.answer: Demand inflation: gaming the dominant-share accounting.

keyTerms.definition: DRF becomes max-min fair sharing of the one resource.
The degenerate case.

recall.question: One resource only. What is DRF?
recall.answer: DRF becomes max-min fair sharing of the one resource.

keyTerms.definition: Cuts max wait vs FIFO on mixed workloads.
Where DRF wins.

recall.question: State the DRF-vs-FIFO hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: DRF cuts max wait vs FIFO on mixed workloads. Report both.

keyTerms.definition: Achieved FLOP/s divided by peak FLOP/s.
Achieved FLOP/s divided by peak FLOP/s.

recall.question: Define MFU.
recall.answer: MFU = achieved FLOP/s divided by peak FLOP/s.

keyTerms.definition: MFU is measured for E52 at a value of 48.1%.
Bubble-free projection for E52 is shown at 65.8%.

recall.question: What is the MFU value for E52?
recall.answer: The MFU value for E52 is 48.1%. The bubble-free projection is 65.8%.

keyTerms.definition: Or inflated FLOP counting: the numerator grew without speeding the run.
Grew.

recall.question: MFU rises but the run slows. What inflated the numerator?
recall.answer: Recomputation (or inflated FLOP counting). The numerator grew without speeding the run.

keyTerms.definition: MFU halves: same achieved, double peak.
The cause.

recall.question: Peak doubles. What happens to MFU at fixed achieved?
recall.answer: MFU halves (same achieved, double peak).

keyTerms.definition: Explain over half the MFU gap.
Report the split.

recall.question: State the attribution hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: the top two taxes explain over half the MFU gap. Report the split.

keyTerms.definition: Per-GPU MTBF / GPU count.
Mean time between failures.

recall.question: Write the cluster MTBF formula.
recall.answer: Cluster MTBF = per-GPU MTBF / GPU count.

keyTerms.definition: The amount of time equal to 102.7 hours for E57.
E57 has about 7 failures per 30-day run.

recall.question: How many failures does E57 have per 30-day run?
recall.answer: E57 has about 7 failures per 30-day run.

keyTerms.definition: A property that, when broken, means failures stop being separate and start depending on each other.
Describes failures that occur together, as shown by rack power events that trigger multiple failures at once.

recall.question: What happens when independence breaks?
recall.answer: Failures become correlated. The text gives rack power events as an example of one cause that leads to multiple failures.

keyTerms.definition: GPU-hours per failure here.

recall.question: N = 4096. What is the MTBF?

keyTerms.definition: Exceed the independent prediction.
Report both.

recall.question: State the correlation hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: correlated failures exceed the independent prediction. Report both.
